 Chris Godwin failed to catch his only target in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
 Godwin has fallen off the map this year, but forces beyond his control caused this goose egg. The Bucs did not complete a pass and only attempted three in total. With their defense terrorizing Michael Penix, Tampa Bay leaned on their ground game to an absurd degree. Emeka Egbuka is working through a foot injury and didn’t play today. Godwin will return to the WR4/5 border if he’s back for Week 9. Godwin would have some FLEX appeal if the Bucs are without their No. 1 receiver versus the Bears next week.
 -  Kyle Dvorchak

 Chris Godwin caught 4-of-5 targets for 27 yards in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers. 
 That might not look like much, especially with Emeka Egbuka on the shelf, but it was actually a 45 percent target share in a game where the Bucs attempted just 11 passes in a 43-13 victory. Godwin also had a score called back by a Bucky Irving illegal shift. Promising in theory, we suppose, though Godwin has not cracked 40 yards receiving since Week 2. He has not reached 50 all year. It feels like he will have to get more involved at some point, but then again, this team has a lot of young receiving talent. Godwin’s WR4 prospects are hanging on by a thread heading into Week 8 against the Falcons.

 Wide Receiver 
 #14 
 Chris Godwin caught 4-of-8 targets for 37 yards in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers. 
 Godwin’s eight targets today go down as a season-high, but he failed to make much of his opportunities, per usual. The veteran wideout hasn’t hit 50 receiving yards in a game this year and is still looking for his first touchdown of the season. With Emeka Egbuka pulling away as the team’s WR1, there isn’t much volume headed Godwin’s way. With Jalon Daniels likely to make another start next week, Godwin is tumbling down the WR4 ranks ahead of Week 7.

 Chris Godwin caught all three targets for 37 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 5 win over the Cowboys. 
 Godwin’s three targets finished tied for fourth on the team behind Emeka Egbuka, Cade Otton, and Kenny Gainwell on a night backup quarterback Jalon Daniels attempted only 25 passes. Week 5 now marks the fourth game in five tries in which Godwin was held to four targets or fewer, leaving the veteran wide receiver completely unusable in a fantasy setting, for the time being. He can safely be stashed on benches ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Steelers.

 Chris Godwin caught 6-of-7 targets for 31 yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers. 
 UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels made his first career start and leaned on Godwin for some easy completions. Godwin led the team in catches and targets, though Cade Otton surprisingly led the way in yards with 37. Godwin set new season highs in targets and catches. The Bucs are operating an incredibly low-wattage offense without Baker Mayfield, but Godwin could continue to see enough work to return WR4 numbers in PPR leagues. He will put that to the test versus the Cowboys in Week 5.

 The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports that the Colts informed Daniel Jones that they are not trading him by Tuesday’s deadline.
 Jones successfully returned from last year’s season-ending Achilles tendon rupture, but his play has been negatively impacted by it. With two young quarterbacks on the roster, it would seemingly make sense to trade Jones to get an extended look at either Riley Leonard and/or Anthony Richardson. Apparently, the Colts disagree. We have no way of knowing whether Pelissero’s report is a hardball negotiation tactic by the Colts’ front office, but we will have an answer to that question in the next couple of days.
 -  Nic Bodiford

 Quinshon Judkins rushed 15 times for 43 yards in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
 Judkins was hit at or behind the line of scrimmage constantly, resulting in a dreadful yards per carry of 2.9. This was particularly painful for fantasy managers when he got near the end zone. Judkins was stuffed from the one- and three-yard line on separate drives. He also ceded receiving work to Dylan Sampson. Judkins was targeted once while Sampson saw six opportunities through the air. Without receiving work to buoy his poor rushing days, Judkins is tumbling down the RB2 ranks. He’ll be on the RB2/3 border for his Week 10 matchup with the Texans. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak

 Drew Lock completed 19-of-28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ 17-3, Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding 16 yards on five carries.
 Lock appeared to suffer discomfort in the third quarter following an incomplete pass attempt, holding his side or oblique and grimacing in pain as he made his way to sideline. He would get checked in the medical tent but returned without missing a down. Lock looked poised in the pocket and in control of the offense throughout, leaning on his alpha wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba early before the team went into preservation mode with a sizable lead in the second half. Lock could be looking at another start or two, pending the length of recovery from a cracked rib for Sam Darnold. His next start will come against arguably the worst defense in the league in the Raiders in Week 10, where Lock will border streamer status in deeper leagues.
 -  Mark Garcia

 Jordan Love completed 23-of-29 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns in the Packers’ 45-27, Week 9 win over the Patriots.
 As has been the case for much of the season, big plays were the name of the game for Love. Love aired the ball out at will against a helpless Patriots defense, going 6-for-9 on passes of 20-plus air yards for 235 yards and a touchdown. Love connected with Matthew Golden on multiple long plays in the first quarter, completing passes of 43 and 49 yards, and found him in the end zone for a five-yard score. Love’s longest touchdown pass of the day came in the third quarter when he connected with Christian Watson for a 39-yard-score immediately after the Packers recovered a fumble by Rhamondre Stevenson. Love and the Packers boast arguably the most explosive passing attack in the league, and both Watson and Golden continue to look like premier threats while also being versatile in other areas of the field. Love and the Vikings will have their work cut out for them next week at home against the Vikings, but he will remain in the QB1 mix.
 -  Zachary Krueger

 Trey McBride caught 7-of-8 targets for 54 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.
 The lone incompletion directed toward McBride came on the team’s final play of the game when the veteran tight end was unable to corral an end zone target that was thrown slightly behind him on fourth and goal. McBride combined with alpha wide receiver Michael Wilson to account for 15 targets on 30 Minshew pass attempts, something we’d expect to continue forward give the current state of the team. The Cardinals get another difficult matchup against the Rams in Week 10, where McBride will remain a surefire TE1 in fantasy circles.

 Michael Wilson caught 6-of-7 targets for 60 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks. 
 The lone Gardner Minshew incompletion directed toward Wilson was an end zone target late in the fourth quarter, a miss that would have salvaged a usable fantasy outing for the veteran receiver. Wilson was responsible for nearly one third of the total offensive output from a Cardinals offense that was held to under 200 yards by the stingy Seattle defense, finishing second on the team in targets behind the eight of tight end Trey McBride. He remains an upside WR2 ahead of another difficult test against the Rams in Week 10.

 Tyler Allgeier rushed 17 times for 46 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks, gaining zero additional yards on two receptions.
 In what was the first game as the clear starter for the Cardinals in the absence of both Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight, Allgeier was contained to only 2.7 yards per carry as the offense managed under 200 yards of total offense against the stingy Seattle defense. Fantasy managers that were quick to scoop Allgeier off of waivers heading into Week 9 are surely to be disappointed with the returns, particularly considering Knight had largely outperformed the former prior to missing Week 9 with a concussion. Expect a near-even split backfield once Knight returns, which appears likely to be in Week 10 when the Cardinals face another difficult test in the Rams.
